Output: `/home/mara/cwe-bench/pipelines/stacking/out/screener/3759.json`

Trust decision: gatekeeper's mandatory inbound header deny-list (`swift/common/middleware/gatekeeper.py:51-55`) omits the update headers, so client-supplied `X-Container-Host`/`X-Delete-At-Host`/`X-Account-*` are copied verbatim (`swift/proxy/controllers/obj.py:501`) and used as outbound update targets by the object/container server.

`pattern_fit`: injection_only — one fix site, no O2 site, no O8 route (gatekeeper is auto-inserted first; bulk/formpost subrequests whitelist headers).

Strongest lever: the must-keep-working headers that share these prefixes (`X-Delete-At`, `X-Container-Read/Write/Sync-To`) vs. the anchored-regex fix — an over-broad or single-name fix breaks or misses.

Biggest red flag: `single_site` (plus `protection_documented_without_exceptions` — gatekeeper is documented as always present, so no route can be argued out of scope).
